theses.one_liner: Pony AI has lost 73% in a year and still trades at 18x TTM sales on a business whose own unit economics describe 20-30% gross margin, while TTM free cash flow is -1.73bn RMB (-198% margin) funded by 65% YoY share growth.
theses.thesis: The equity is now down 73% over twelve months and 27% in the last month, yet it remains priced as a fleet land-grab: 2.21bn USD market cap on 869m RMB TTM revenue is 18.0x sales and 9.4x EV/sales. The operating reality in the same filings is an operating margin of -290%, operating cash outflow of 1.42bn RMB and free cash flow of -1.73bn RMB over the trailing four quarters, worsening each fiscal year (FY2023 -854m, FY2024 -714m, FY2025 -1.46bn RMB FCF) while the share count grew 65%. The bull case rests on a fleet target of 3,500 robotaxis by end-2026 and a Gen-4 hardware cost-down, both of which are promises about 2027 unit economics rather than current P&L. What has changed in the last month is the tape, not the fundamentals: the stock broke to 2% of its 52-week range, so the short is no longer contrarian - it is now a crowded, well-covered short into a catalyst-rich quarter.
bear_points: TTM revenue 869m RMB against free cash flow of -1.73bn RMB and an operating margin of -290%: every incremental vehicle adds capex and depreciation before it adds profit.
Burn is scaling with the fleet, not away from it: FCF went -854m (FY2023) to -714m (FY2024) to -1.46bn RMB (FY2025), and the trailing four quarters are worse than any single fiscal year.
Dilution is the funding model: shares outstanding grew 65.3% YoY, which is how a -1.7bn RMB cash deficit gets financed at a 2.21bn USD valuation.
18.0x TTM sales and 9.4x EV/sales for a hardware-adjacent business guiding to 20-30% unit gross margin leaves no room for the margin to be anything less than the top of that range.
risks_to_short: Sell-side is uniformly constructive and targets sit far above spot: Goldman Sachs Buy with a HK202.4 target (2026-10-08, cut but maintained), UBS Buy with a 20 USD target (2026-09-02). A single Uber Europe deployment headline can move a 2.21bn USD cap violently - the Uber agreement already covers 2,000+ vehicles across five European cities with 4,000 more under negotiation.
Cash is not obviously short: the company funds the gap from the equity market, and a capital raise at a higher price is the standard squeeze mechanism for this kind of story stock.
Already -73% in twelve months and at 2% of its 52-week range: the easy part of the de-rating has happened, and the borrow (8.0% of float, 7.0 days to cover) is no longer cheap.

theses.one_liner: WeRide trades at 12.4x TTM sales, burned 1.29bn RMB of operating cash in FY2025 on 666m RMB of revenue, and the growth now arriving is driver-assistance kits rather than robotaxi fares.
theses.thesis: WeRide's revenue is growing fast (+84% TTM) but the composition is the issue: the step-change came from L2++ ADAS kits (about 30k units in 2Q26, revenue up nearly 2,600% YoY) rather than from robotaxi operations, while operating cash flow was -156% of revenue and FY2025 operating burn was 1.29bn RMB against 666m RMB of revenue. The company funds that with a 19% YoY increase in shares. At 1.44bn USD the equity is 12.4x TTM sales - not cheap for a company whose incremental revenue is ADAS kits with automotive-supplier economics, and the robotaxi fleet (1,800 vehicles, targeting 2,600 by end-2026) still runs at a loss per city. bear_points: At 12.4x TTM sales, operating cash flow is -156% of revenue and FY2025 burn was 1.29bn RMB against 666m RMB of revenue; the trailing year shows no improvement in the cash profile.
The revenue mix is shifting toward L2++ ADAS kits - an automotive-supplier business with supplier margins - while the robotaxi fleet that justifies the narrative still needs city-by-city capital.
Fleet targets are the growth story (1,800 robotaxis today to 2,600 by end-2026) and every vehicle added is capex before it is revenue.

Overseas expansion is asset-light - about 50% revenue share with Uber-type partners in the Middle East and Europe - which is the structure a short least wants to see work.
Seven of the ten most recent documents are Chinese broker transcripts with a positive tilt, and the December 2026 robotaxi target is a scheduled catalyst against the position.

theses.thesis: Zai Lab's problem is the shape of the P&L rather than the science. TTM revenue fell 3% to 3.51bn RMB while free cash flow stayed at -1.13bn RMB (-32% margin) and the operating margin is -59%; the company has burned 1.13-1.71bn RMB of free cash every year since 2023. Into that, it sold 250m USD of equity on 2026-10-22 at 22.04 USD per ADS - roughly 10% of the enlarged share capital, priced at a discount to the prior close. Meanwhile the stock has re-rated 31% in three months and 40% year-to-date on the ESMO zocilurtatug pelitecan dataset (ORR 81.8%, 6-month PFS 81.9% in 1L ES-SCLC), which is a 2027-2028 revenue proposition. The short case is the gap between a pipeline-driven multiple and an equity-funded burn: 6.6x TTM sales for a company whose marketed portfolio is shrinking, with the next leg of the story requiring three registrational trials to start before the end of 2026.
bear_points: Revenue is going backwards (-3% TTM, after -6% in H1 product revenue) while the multiple has expanded 31% in three months on pipeline data.
Free cash flow has been negative every year since 2023 (-1.60bn, -1.71bn, -1.24bn RMB) and the trailing year is -1.13bn RMB; the 250m USD PIPE is a funding event, not a validation.
Operating margin of -59% with a 4.2-year runway means the company returns to the equity market before the pipeline pays for itself.
11.3 days to cover on 6.5% short interest: the position is already crowded relative to a 97m share float.

J.P.Morgan remains OW and expects a global Phase 3 to start in 2026 (2026-10-23).
Balance sheet: 12% net cash to market cap plus the fresh PIPE proceeds removes any near-term funding pressure, so there is no forced-event timeline for the short.

theses.one_liner: Kanzhun screens as a top-five short because of size and crowding, not because the business is failing: 52% free-cash-flow margin and +15% revenue growth against a 6.4x sales multiple, after a 31% one-month rally.
theses.thesis: This is the clearest example in the book of a name that ranks on tradability rather than on a broken business. Kanzhun generates a 52% free-cash-flow margin on 8.66bn RMB of TTM revenue with +15% revenue growth, has net cash, pays a 2.0% dividend and trades at 12.1x trailing and 12.1x forward earnings - and it just rallied 31% in a month to 7.83bn USD. What the screen likes is the other side: 88m USD of daily turnover (the most liquid name in the book), 6.4% short interest and 6.0 days to cover, and a P/S multiple that is high in absolute terms because the market capitalises a recruitment platform's margins, not its revenue. The short case, such as it is, is that a cyclical hiring recovery is already in the price after a 27% six-month run, and that the reported 87% YoY share-count growth (which looks like a share-class artefact and needs verification before it is used) undermines the buyback narrative. Read this as a crowding and valuation trade, not a thesis about a deteriorating company.
bear_points: Valuation is the whole trade: 6.4x TTM sales and 2.8x book for a recruitment marketplace with 15% growth, after a 31% one-month and 27% six-month rally.
Reported dilution of +87% YoY sits awkwardly against the buyback and dividend story - the figure is probably a share-class artefact, but until it is reconciled it is an open question, not a support.
Revenue growth of 15% is a deceleration from a 20% three-year CAGR, and the incremental growth is coming from a hiring cycle that is itself the risk.

A 52% FCF margin with net cash means the company can buy back stock into a short indefinitely; there is no solvency clock here.
Huatai's non-AI internet re-rating call (2026-10-13) explicitly names BOSS Zhipin as a beneficiary of rotation out of AI names - the marginal buyer has a thesis.

theses.thesis: This is a shell-shaped story rather than a business. Revenue was 4m USD in FY2026 (down 6%, and down from 5m two years earlier), operating margin -78%, free cash flow -4m USD, and the runway calculation returns 0.1 years - the company is close to its last dollar at the current burn. The AlphaEngine record is 20 documents and every one of them is a filing, including a 'STOP ORDER' notice dated 2026-10-15 - there is no broker coverage, no transcript and no analyst number anywhere in the bundle. When a 4m USD revenue company trades at 322m with a sub-year runway and a regulatory stop order in its own filing stack, the right posture is to treat the quote as unreliable rather than to underwrite a fundamental short.
bear_points: 4m USD of revenue against a 322m USD market cap (87.5x sales, 206x book) with a -78% operating margin and -103% free-cash-flow margin.
0.1-year runway on the screen's own cash-burn calculation: the company needs capital, and the only capital available to a 4m-revenue shell is more equity.
The document trail is filings only, including an SEC stop order (2026-10-15) - a liquidity and eligibility risk that no fundamental model captures.
risks_to_short: The quote is not realisable: 12m USD of daily turnover on a 322m cap with a 6m-share float means borrow is either unavailable or recalls without notice, and a stop order can make the position impossible to exit.
A 884% twelve-month return is the signature of a promotional float, not of a valuation gap - shorting into that with no borrow is a financing decision, not a research decision.
Any reverse merger, capital injection or relisting announcement re-rates the shell instantly and has nothing to do with the P&L.
catalysts: Resolution or escalation of the 2026-10-15 stop order and any subsequent filing (AlphaEngine 公告, 2026-10-15 / 2026-10-22).

theses.one_liner: Full Truck Alliance is a 34% free-cash-flow-margin freight marketplace at 14.8x earnings and 4.9x sales; it ranks in the book on liquidity, not on weakness.
theses.thesis: YMM is the second clearest case of a name that scores high because it is tradable, not because it is broken. The marketplace generates a 34% free-cash-flow margin on 12.70bn RMB of revenue, has grown revenue at a 21% three-year CAGR, trades at 14.8x trailing and 11.1x forward earnings with 1.3x book and a 2.4% dividend, and holds net cash. What the screen sees is 55m USD of daily turnover, a 2.2% short interest that leaves room to build, and a stock that is -34% over twelve months and 15% up its 52-week range after a four-month flat patch. The honest short here is a growth-deceleration and mix trade: revenue growth has slowed to 5%, the brokerage and financial-services lines are shrinking (-15% and -25% YoY in 2Q26) while the higher-margin transaction line grows 33%, and the market is paying 4.9x sales for a company whose incremental growth is now regulatory and cycle dependent. It is not a solvency short and should not be sized as one.
bear_points: Revenue growth has decelerated to 5% from a 21% three-year CAGR, and the mix is shifting: transaction services +33% versus brokerage -15% and financial services -25% in 2Q26.
At 4.9x sales and 14.8x earnings the stock is priced for the marketplace margin structure to persist while the lending book shrinks and incentives rise.
Reported dilution of +71% YoY against a 400m USD shareholder-return programme needs reconciling before it is used either way - the two cannot both be true at face value.
risks_to_short: The company is buying back stock and pays a dividend (2026 400m USD return programme, Citi 2026-09-03) with a 34% FCF margin - a short competes with the company's own bid.
Every broker in the bundle is constructive: Citi Buy with 14, HSBC Buy with 15 (2026-08-24) against an 8.42 close, and management guides 4Q order growth back to low-to-mid teens.
2.2% short interest means there is no crowding to unwind and no forced-cover catalyst - the position has no technical tailwind.
catalysts: Q3 2026 results and the 4Q order-growth inflection management has guided to (HSBC 2026-08-24; Citi 2026-09-03).

theses.one_liner: VNET has fallen 61% in a month while funding a 5.9bn RMB free-cash-flow deficit with 105% YoY share growth; the borrow is now 27.6% of float, so the trade has moved from under-owned to crowded.
theses.thesis: The fundamental case has not changed, but the price has. VNET spent 5.93bn RMB of free cash flow over the trailing four quarters while operating cash flow was 16% of revenue, covering the gap with a 105% YoY increase in shares and net debt; capex on the AIDC buildout is the whole story and it is being financed from the equity and credit markets. Revenue growth of 15% and a 0.7x sales multiple look cheap until the balance sheet is brought in. What has changed since the last book is the tape and the ownership: the stock is down 61% in a month and 59% in a year, sits at 3% of its 52-week range, and short interest has risen to 27.6% of float with 8.5 days to cover. A short that was right and is now consensus is a different risk: the remaining downside is the next financing, and the upside is a 38.1% strategic holder (a CATL affiliate) with a reason to support the equity.
bear_points: Free cash flow of -5.93bn RMB on 10.67bn RMB of revenue: the AIDC buildout consumes capital faster than operations generate it, and the trailing year is worse than either of the last two fiscal years.
105% YoY share growth is the funding mechanism, and every incremental megawatt of contracted capacity front-loads more of it.
Short interest at 27.6% of a 172m-share float with 8.5 days to cover: the position is crowded, and crowded shorts pay for the privilege.
risks_to_short: Catalyst risk is concentrated on the upside: a CATL affiliate (PJ Millennium) closed the purchase of 38.1% of VNET for about 942m USD ahead of schedule (Citi 2026-09-21), bringing cheap power and a strategic anchor holder.

Order momentum is strong - 862MW of new orders year-to-date including 347MW in 2Q26, with full-year wholesale guidance of 1,000-1,100MW (Goldman Sachs 2026-09-03; Nomura 2026-09-11). Targets sit at 11.3-14 USD against a 3.77 close.
Morgan Stanley's Ulanqab power-usage series showed Q3 +15% QoQ with a 4Q recovery expected (2026-10-09) - the operating data the market watches is still growing.
catalysts: Q3 2026 results and 4Q order intake (Morgan Stanley 2026-10-09; Nomura 2026-09-11).
Financing terms for the remaining AIDC capacity - the next equity or debt raise (Goldman Sachs 2026-09-03: no equity raise planned this year, net debt/EBITDA held under 6x).
Timetable for the CATL-affiliate stake to translate into power-cost synergies (Citi 2026-09-21).

theses.one_liner: Daqo screen-ranks as a short on a -50% free-cash-flow margin, but it holds about 2.06bn USD of cash and no debt against a 744m USD market cap - the balance sheet, not the P&L, is the trade.
theses.thesis: The screen is flagging a real operating deterioration and a balance sheet that makes the short dangerous. Daqo's TTM revenue fell 21% to 3.91bn RMB with a -21% gross margin and -41% operating margin, free cash flow of -1.97bn RMB (-50% margin), after a brutal FY2024 (-5.89bn RMB FCF, -55% operating margin). Polysilicon is being sold below cash cost and the company is retiring 30-40k tonnes of capacity. But it holds roughly 2.06bn USD of cash and equivalents with zero debt against a 744m USD market cap, which is why it trades at 0.17x book: the equity is a call option on polysilicon prices plus a liquidation floor. Shorting a company whose net cash exceeds its market capitalisation means betting that the cash gets burned before the cycle turns - and at 10.99 the stock is already down 61% in a year and 66% year-to-date, at 1% of its 52-week range, with 10.2% short interest and 11.2 days to cover. Goldman Sachs cut to Sell with a 10 USD target in August; that call is now essentially at spot.
bear_points: Revenue -21% TTM and -47% on a three-year CAGR with a -21% gross margin: polysilicon is being sold below cash cost and the 3Q26 gross margin was still -31%.
Free cash flow of -1.97bn RMB over the trailing year, after -5.89bn in FY2024, is the mechanism by which a large net cash pile disappears.
The equity trades at 0.17x book precisely because the market does not believe the cash survives the downcycle.
risks_to_short: Net cash of about 2.06bn USD against a 744m USD market cap with zero debt (3Q26 transcript, 2026-10-27): the downside is floored by liquidation value and any polysilicon price recovery goes straight to equity.
